articles.title: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
articles.summary:
NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom, K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research, Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies.
As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance.
NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance.
Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box. They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services.
Learn more about NVIDIA Dynamo.

articles.title: Launching the Vite Ecosystem Fund
articles.summary:
Launching the Vite Ecosystem Fund
Cloudflare is distributing the first $301,300 of the Vite Ecosystem Fund to 44 projects and maintainers across the Vite ecosystem.
When VoidZero joined Cloudflare, we committed $1 million to strengthen the open source ecosystem around Vite. This round is just the start.
Sponsoring open source has always mattered, but now AI has made funding urgent.
AI is changing open source
AI has made open source more valuable while triggering more maintainer burnout. Previously, contributing to a project through either an issue or pull request meant you cared about it. In return, maintainers would review and provide feedback. AI changed the social contract of open source. Anyone can now create and submit AI-authored pull requests.
The most visible result is the influx of pull requests. As the number of PRs has gone up, the number of maintainers reviewing them has stayed constant. So each maintainer’s workload has grown.
During reviews, maintainers often find themselves speaking with an agent and not a person like they used to. If that’s the case, then why not cut out the middleman? Maintainers now have their own agents they can prompt to produce better results since they have more knowledge of the codebase.
AI has raised the pressure to produce. It’s made it easier for maintainers to ship features, performance improvements, and bug fixes that would not have been done otherwise. But it’s also made it easy for other projects to do the same. When another proj…

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: Google DeepMind’s AI Agents Make 1024-Bit RSA Keys Cheaper to Attack
articles.summary:
Google DeepMind says AI agents working under human supervision have found two ways to reduce the cost of attacking 1024-bit RSA cryptosystems.
The research, conducted with cryptographers from UC San Diego and Inria, indicates that attacks on legacy RSA-1024 require less computation than previously assumed.
“In practice, these results only affect obsolete 1024-bit RSA systems, and modern encryption protocols, which almost universally use 2048-bit or larger keys, remain secure,” said Pushmeet Kohli, VP at Google DeepMind and chief scientist at Google Cloud.
The first finding involves digital signatures and padding, the preset data that many signature standards add to a message to bring it to a fixed block size. Padding was known to make forgery harder, but its value against an attacker who can choose what gets signed was unclear.
DeepMind determined that it depends on the share of the signed block the attacker controls. “Once they control roughly half of the block or more, padding adds no protection at all,” Kohli explained.
According to the accompanying paper, this applies to the PKCS#1 v1.5 format used by the PKCS#11 signing interface of cryptographic devices such as hardware security modules (HSMs).
In a sandboxed test, the agents re-ran an earlier academic forgery attack on the same 1024-bit key, cutting CPU time 3.5-fold. The first forgery took 391 CPU core-years, versus 1,380 in the original study.

articles.title: Ukraine dismantles crypto scam network that stole €4.3 million
articles.summary:
Ukrainian law enforcement arrested four suspects in a case involving the theft of more than €4.3 million using a network of cryptocurrency investment scam call centers.
In these fraud schemes (also known as romance baiting or pig butchering scams), criminals lure targets through social media, dating sites, and messaging apps into fake investment schemes, stealing their money instead of investing the funds as promised.
The investigation involved Ukraine's Cyber Police Department, the Main Investigation Department of the National Police of Ukraine, and German law enforcement authorities.
According to Ukraine's Cyber Police, the suspects used phone calls and messaging apps to build victims' trust through social engineering and trick them into investing in cryptocurrency, shares, and other financial instruments through fraudulent online trading platforms.
The crime ring targeted potential victims across the European Union, stealing more than €4.3 million from 135 German victims.
"They assisted victims in opening accounts on cryptocurrency exchanges, purchasing digital assets and transferring them to accounts controlled by the criminal organisation. In some cases, the suspects also gained access to victims' online banking accounts," the Ukrainian Cyber Police said.
"The proceeds of crime were subsequently moved through bank accounts, cryptocurrency exchanges and transit wallets, converted and distributed among members of the criminal organisation."

articles.title: Affaire Jensen Huang : quelles conséquences pour Nvidia, au-delà du scandale ? — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Lundi 9 novembre, cinq minutes à peine après la clôture de la Bourse américaine, un cabinet d’avocats déposait une plainte en nom collectif (class action) contre Nvidia et son CEO devant le tribunal fédéral de San Jose. Une réactivité millimétrée face au décrochage du titre, qui venait de céder 4,27 % en une journée pour clôturer à 178,67 dollars, à rebours d’un secteur des semi-conducteurs pourtant dans le vert.
La veille, Jensen Huang avait publiquement reconnu une liaison extra-conjugale : une relation nouée avec Alice Huang, cadre chez le client asiatique Megaspeed, que le contre-espionnage américain soupçonne d’agir pour le compte de Pékin.
Depuis cet aveu, la crise a pris une tournure très politique, comme on pouvait s’y attendre. Donald Trump a affirmé lundi avoir échangé par téléphone avec le dirigeant : Jensen Huang lui aurait juré ignorer tout des activités présumées de sa compagne, une version que le président américain dit croire, tout en confirmant que le FBI a ouvert un dossier.
Tandis que Pékin balaie des accusations jugées sans fondement, le conseil d’administration de Nvidia assure n’avoir aucun indice laissant penser que des secrets industriels ont fuité.
Pour autant, aucune date butoir n’a été fixée pour son audit interne, et le patron, qui promettait dans sa lettre d’excuses aux salariés de coopérer pleinement, conserve les rênes du groupe en attendant.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.title: Mort imminente : 50 témoins ont dessiné leurs visions, quatre formes reviennent sans cesse
articles.summary:
Mort imminente : 50 témoins ont dessiné leurs visions, quatre formes reviennent sans cesse
Visio, scans et statistiques en Python : la science cartographie le tunnel de lumière
Le fameux tunnel existe bien dans les souvenirs de ceux qui ont frôlé la mort. Il n’est pourtant qu’un décor parmi d’autres. Des chercheurs ont demandé à 50 personnes de dessiner leur expérience de mort imminente. Dans leurs croquis, quatre architectures reviennent avec une régularité troublante, et la couleur de chaque scène semble dictée par sa forme. Une cartographie de l’invisible qui intrigue jusqu’aux concepteurs de réalité virtuelle.
Une lumière aveuglante, la sensation de flotter au-dessus de son corps, un couloir obscur… Depuis des siècles, les expériences de mort imminente (EMI) se racontent avec les mêmes mots, faute de mieux. France Lerner, chercheuse en neurophénoménologie à l'Université de Haïfa, a choisi le crayon. Avec son équipe, elle a fait dessiner à 50 personnes les espaces qu'elles avaient traversés, dans une étude publiée le 15 octobre par la revue Frontiers in Psychology. Les participants ont décrit 112 scènes, dont 108 se rangent dans quatre familles géométriques.
Le phénomène est loin d'être rare : jusqu'à un survivant d'arrêt cardiaque sur cinq rapporte une EMI, selon une synthèse publiée en 2025.

articles.title: Make a Robot Arm Feel Weightless with NVIDIA Holoscan 5 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Picture guiding a robot arm by hand while its motors supply just enough torque to support its weight and keep the robot upright. This simple interaction, a useful starting point for robots that learn by demonstration, manipulate objects, or work alongside people, depends on a gravity-compensation loop.
Building such a loop is only possible by continuously calculating the inverse dynamics of the system based on precise models of all the links of the robot arm, their dimensions, masses, and moments of inertia. This calculation, which needs to be done rapidly with low jitter, requires knowing the current state of the robot, so gravity-comp demos are an excellent proof of life for both the robot model and the runtime that’s executing these algorithms.
NVIDIA Holoscan 5 introduced robotic control alongside streamlined sensor processing. In this tutorial, we’ll build custom Holoscan SDK operators and wire them into a graph. We’ll test the code on a real robot and use the Holoscan SDK’s built-in Nsight Systems annotations to inspect latency and jitter.
This walkthrough has been tested on Jetson Orin Nano, Jetson Thor, and x86 Ubuntu 24.04 systems.
Why Holoscan?
Holoscan SDK brings low-latency control and high-throughput perception into one programming model, with execution paths designed for CPU- and GPU-based workloads. Its goal is a transparent runtime: minimize avoidable framework overhead while making application execution explicit and inspectable.

articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
How CrossnoKaye grounds physical AI with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Industrial operations present AI challenges that don’t show up in typical enterprise software. In most facilities, plant data and control logic are spread across separate systems from different vendors: programmable logic controllers (PLCs) and distributed control systems (DCS) run the equipment logic, historians record time-series tags under site-specific naming schemes, supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems drive operator screens, and standalone optimization tools or alarm loggers sit on the side. Bolting an external AI agent onto that stack rarely works well in practice. Each system uses its own naming conventions. The logic that actually governs how equipment behaves (the control sequences, state machines, and safety interlocks) is locked inside proprietary controller code that an external tool can’t inspect. Giving a bolt-on agent access across multiple operational technology (OT) systems also means distributing credentials across the plant network.
CrossnoKaye took a different approach to bring physical AI to heavy industry using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Its software-defined automation platform, ATLAS, connects live plant data and AI reasoning to closed-loop control of the equipment running food and beverage plants, industrial refrigeration facilities, aggregates quarries, and manufacturing sites. articles.title: Over 3 Million People Hit by Frontline Education Data Breach
articles.summary:
Frontline Education has informed the Indiana Attorney General’s Office that a data breach it suffered in August affected more than 3 million people.
The K-12 school administration software provider puts the total number of affected individuals at 3,085,266. That is well over twice the figure from the company’s earlier filings with several other states, which added up to roughly 1.3 million.
Frontline says the attackers got into part of its environment by exploiting a vulnerability in a third-party software product. The company detected the intrusion on August 14 and says the attack was fully contained the next day.
The hackers stole the personal information of school district employees and students from two Frontline products: Frontline Central and School Health Management.
The compromised information varies from person to person. It may include names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, driver’s license numbers, passport and other government ID numbers, health insurance information such as Medicaid IDs, and student IDs.
Affected adults in the US are getting two years of free credit monitoring and identity theft protection. Eligible minors are getting free dark web monitoring.
Frontline has not named the exploited third-party product or said who was behind the attack.
No known cybercrime group appears to have taken credit for an attack on the company.

C’est désormais Cadillac qui lance son système SuperCruise en Europe. Ce système permettra au conducteur de lâcher les mains du volant sur autoroute et jusqu’à 130 km/h sur 180 000 km d’autoroute dans 16 pays différents. L’attention du conducteur doit encore rester sur la route, une caméra dotée d’un système de surveillance y veillera. articles.title: Amplifon Americas Data Breach Impacts 1.3 Million
articles.summary:
Amplifon Hearing Health Care has disclosed a data breach impacting the information of more than 1.3 million individuals in the US.
The incident involves Amplifon Americas, the Minneapolis-based arm of the Italian hearing healthcare giant Amplifon, which claims to serve over 80 million members through a nationwide network of thousands of clinics.
According to Amplifon Americas’ data breach notice, hackers broke into its internal systems in January 2026 and copied files from certain systems between January 18 and February 8.
Although it immediately contained the incident and launched an investigation into the attack, Amplifon needed eight months to review the stolen data and determine that personal information was potentially affected.
The review concluded that names, contact information, driver’s license numbers, other government ID numbers, dates of birth, hearing and medical information, dates of service, other health information, and health insurance information were compromised.
For some individuals, Social Security numbers and financial information were also stolen, the company says.
“We are not aware of any fraudulent use of personal information as a result of this incident,” Amplifon notes.
Amplifon’s filing with the Texas Attorney General’s Office reportedly mentions a total of 1,332,826 people being affected nationwide.

A decisão encerra o procedimento original, mas não interrompe automaticamente as investigações e os processos derivados que ainda estejam em andamento.

O ministro também ressaltou que o arquivamento não afeta condenações, absolvições, acordos, recebimentos de denúncias ou outras decisões tomadas em processos autônomos.

articles.title: CPU-Z data reveals impact of the memory crisis: 32GB and 64GB PCs decline, DDR4 makes a comeback

Winners & losers: In what will come as a surprise to nobody, the latest CPU-Z hardware survey has illustrated how having more than 16GB of RAM in a PC is increasingly becoming a luxury. With the AI-driven memory crisis continuing to push DRAM prices through the roof, the number of people with 32GB and 64GB configurations is falling, while DDR4 is making a comeback.
The latest CPU-Z Validator statistics come from hardware configurations users submit to CPU-Z's online Validator database, so it doesn't represent retail sales or all PCs. However, it gives us an idea of what the landscape looks like.
The headline takeaway is that, for the first time ever, RAM capacity on PCs has declined year-over-year. Over the last 3 months, the number of systems with 32GB of RAM is down 2.5%, while the number with 64GB of RAM is down 18%.
During the same period, there's been an increase in PCs with smaller amounts of memory. 16GB was up 12.9%, 8GB jumped 5.5%, and 24GB was up 19.7%. Although 32GB remains the most popular capacity (37.2%), 16GB is now just 4.2 points behind the leader.
Another sign of the times is the RAM Generation chart. The number of PCs with last-generation DDR4 increased 6% YoY to 54.4%, cementing its place at the top. The current-gen DDR5, in second place, was down 2.9% to 32.9%. Both RAM generations have shot up in price, but DDR4 is still the cheaper of the two.

articles.title: Can We Trust AI Agents When Zero Trust Isn’t Really Zero
articles.summary:
This article is brought to you by Queen’s University Belfast.
Several teams around the globe are leveraging AI by creating a task force of agents managed by an orchestrator and creating applications to support risk assessment, client profiling, match making, and information yield with a slight overview of decision making. One of the important components for these agents is to ensure that the logs are managed and historic relevance is not being used to avoid skewing towards same decision making. Thus, the system is expected to keep checkpoints in place where agents are prompted to delete such historic relevance.
However, despite such methodology in place, a future prompt could make the agents bring forward the information that was supposed to be deleted and can be tricked into revealing more information, which is a classic case of context recovery attack. So, the question raised here is: How can we trust that our instructions have been followed? And where is the proof?
There is an element of utilizing zero-trust architectures (ZTA) for orchestrating and managing agentic activity, which simply means all agentic interactions use the core principle of “never trust,” “always verify.” ZTA components include a policy enforcement point (PEP) that has to be trusted to maintain trust across the system, so the question that remains is where is the component of zero-trust, and shall we trust the policies enforced by PEP?

“How do we run our AI agents in production at scale?” is the question every customer eventually asks. It comes bundled with several questions. How do we handle thousands of concurrent user requests securely and confidently? How do we make sure the agents stay reliable under real traffic instead of failing silently? How do we know if an agent still meets the quality and safety standards it passed during testing? What are agent security best practices? Should that be deterministic or non-deterministic? And many more. A proof-of-concept answers none of these, because it is built to show the agent model can do the task, not to survive production traffic, cost pressure, and security review.
That gap between a working prototype and a system that runs reliably, securely, frugally and responsibly at scale, is where most agentic AI initiatives stall, and it is rarely the model’s fault. Every team building an agent tends to rebuild the same scaffolding from scratch: its own routing logic, its own guardrails, its own observability, all applied after the fact rather than built in from the start. The teams need a shared, production-ready architecture that every agent can build on.

articles.title: Plafonné depuis 2016, le Bluetooth va presque quadrupler ses débits en 2027
articles.summary:
Le Bluetooth SIG, consortium de plus de 43 000 entreprises qui pilote la norme, a officialisé le 4 novembre le Bluetooth High Data Throughput, ou HDT. Cette fonction optionnelle de la nouvelle spécification Bluetooth Core 7.0 porte le débit maximal du Bluetooth basse consommation à 7,5 Mbit/s. Ce plafond était resté fixé à 2 Mbit/s depuis Bluetooth 5, présenté fin 2016, qui avait déjà doublé la vitesse de cette déclinaison économe en énergie.
Jusqu’à 7,5 Mbit/s, avec l’audio sans perte en ligne de mire
Pour y parvenir, HDT introduit une nouvelle couche physique, la partie de la norme qui décide comment les bits voyagent sur l’onde radio. Des modulations plus denses font transporter davantage de données à chaque signal. Le débit s’ajuste paquet par paquet entre cinq paliers, de 2 à 7,5 Mbit/s, et un paquet peut dépasser 8 000 octets. Les données perdues sont renvoyées par blocs, avec un mécanisme de correction d’erreurs. Le code qui vérifie l’intégrité des données grimpe par ailleurs de 32 à 64 ou 128 bits.
Les meilleurs écouteurs sans fil en 2026
Le premier usage visé est l’audio haut de gamme, attendu en 2027 : son sans perte et haute résolution, multicanal et spatial. À titre de comparaison, un CD audio débite environ 1,41 Mbit/s, et le SBC, qui transporte la musique en Bluetooth classique, plafonne à 328 kbit/s. HDT pourrait ainsi transporter nativement un son haute résolution et sans perte, là où il faut aujourd’hui passer par des codecs propriétaires comme LDAC ou aptX.

articles.title: Hackers Exploiting ‘SSHole’ Authentication Bypass in OpenSSH
articles.summary:
Threat actors have started exploiting SSHole, a recently patched high-severity authentication bypass vulnerability in OpenSSH.
Tracked as CVE-2026-123158, the flaw is “related to misinterpretation of whether a string is intended to be a password hash” and could let attackers access certain accounts by supplying any password between 257 and 1024 characters.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to access accounts such as root, which should never accept a password.
On certain Linux distributions that use the musl libc implementation with the Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) disabled, such as Alpine, Buildroot, OpenWrt, Yocto, and others, these accounts do accept a password.
This happens because the OpenSSH server (sshd) checks the supplied password by hashing it against a stored password hash associated with the username.
When an account has no password hash, as with root on Alpine (where the field is ‘*’), sshd borrows the salt from another account’s hash to process the login attempt. For passwords longer than 256 bytes, musl’s crypt() function fails and, instead of returning NULL, returns ‘*’. Because that matches the ‘*’ stored for the target account, sshd treats the password as correct.
In Alpine, affected accounts include root, any key-only user created with adduser without a password, the Alpine user in the official tiny-cloud images, and any user coming from a directory service through musl-nscd.

articles.title: The Optical Superhighway For AI
articles.summary:
Exponentially increasing AI compute performance requires exponential interconnect speeds.
There is much disagreement on the timing of the transition from copper interconnects to optical interconnects, but almost everyone agrees we are moving to all-optical interconnects over the next five years.
Optical interconnects already dominate scale-out. Optical interconnects will next move into scale-up by connecting racks in very large pods of hundreds to thousands of XPUs (AI compute units), then optical scale-up will replace copper within the rack.
Today, optical is dominated by pluggable transceivers mostly using single wavelengths (DR) with 2 or 4 fibers. Increasing performance using pluggables would require power-hungry, higher-speed PHYs (physical layer interfaces) and/or more fibers, which will drive up costs because connectors cost more than fibers.
To reduce power and cost while increasing bandwidth, the industry consensus is shifting toward multi-wavelengths per fiber with bidirectionality, using NPO (near-packaged optics), then CPO (co-packaged optics). Alternatives may develop, but the emerging consensus for the future of optical interconnect appears to be OCI-MSA.
OCI-MSA (Optical Compute Interconnect Multi-Source Agreement) is an industry consortium recently formed for an open, interoperable optical interconnect spec for AI scale-up. Founding members include AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and OpenAI. In that mix are both GPU giants, the largest maker of custom …

Online publishing platform Medium on Monday launched a new app, called TK, which aims to bring AI technology deeper into the writing process. The idea behind TK is to make it easier to turn ideas into written words by incorporating an AI assistant into the editor itself, allowing users to ask for help by typing “@TK” followed by their request or prompt.
In publishing and journalism, the term “TK” serves as a placeholder used to mark where missing information can be added later. The “TK” stands for “to come,” but uses a “K” instead of “C” as there are few English words where the “tk” letter combination exists, making it stand out more easily in written text where it could be caught by proofreaders.
In Medium’s app, TK takes on a new role as it tries to help users fill in the blanks.
The company suggests the AI assistant could help answer questions that you might normally have to switch to another tab to quickly look up, like how many days are in a particular month. In addition, Medium says TK will ship with particular skills for editorial feedback, headline feedback, and others that could match your draft to the style guide for Medium publications.

Of the 16 WOLED sets from 2020 to 2023 in that group, 14 came out with what the outlet calls edge rot. That covers anything from a stray dead pixel or two to dark clusters chewing along the borders of the panel.
Unlike burn-in, edge rot has nothing to do with what's on screen, so watching varied content won't head it off. RTINGS' best guess, after talking to industry experts, points to the thin protective seal around each panel. Small flaws in it may let moisture creep in over time.
Older panels took the biggest hit. Among the ten TVs built on LG Display's earlier WBC panels, only the 2022 LG A2 escaped untouched. Anyone eyeing a used CX or C1 should keep that in mind. Before buying, it's worth pulling up a plain white or gray screen and checking the edges for dark specks.

The model pairs a 120B-parameter hybrid Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language backbone with 12B active parameters and a C-RADIO vision encoder. MTN South Africa’s customers are consuming more mobile data than ever, but the country’s second-largest mobile operator is finding it difficult to translate that demand into revenue growth.
Data revenue grew by 4.7% in the first nine months of 2026, improving to 6% in the third quarter, according to the group’s latest trading update. Yet service revenue rose by just 1% year-on-year (YoY) over the nine months and was flat in the quarter.
The disconnect highlights a broader challenge for African telecoms operators, as growing internet use does not necessarily translate into stronger financial returns. Operators must monetise data demand while customers face affordability pressures and new forms of connectivity compete with traditional mobile services.
MTN Group chief executive officer (CEO) Ralph Mupita acknowledged that the business remains short of its growth ambitions. “While MTN SA’s service revenue was flat in Q3 2026 and up 1.0% YoY, it remains below our medium-term target,” he said in the statement. “We were however encouraged by the month-on-month improvement in prepaid trends.”
The figures reveal a gap between the data moving across MTN’s network and the revenue it generates from customers. Network traffic rose 27.9% during the nine months, while average monthly data use among postpaid customers rose 31.9% to 32.8GB. Prepaid data consumption also climbed 28.9% to 5.2GB a month.

articles.title: Real-time state has a cost your memory bill won’t show
articles.summary:
Real-time state has a cost your memory bill won’t show
Real-time applications often combine tools with distinct roles. A typical setup might use Kafka to handle events, Flink to process them, Redis to serve the latest state, and a database to maintain the system of record. Applications that use vector search may add a vector store, too.
This division of responsibilities offers flexibility and independent scaling. It also creates costs when data moves between components or when overlapping state is maintained in more than one place.
“The copies to question are those maintained largely because processing happens in one system and applications read the results from another.”
Some of those copies are necessary. Replicas protect against failures, checkpoints help systems recover, and durable event logs preserve history. They’re worth paying for. The copies to question are those maintained largely because processing happens in one system and applications read the results from another.
Take a velocity counter tracking a payment card’s transactions over the past five minutes. Flink calculates the count and maintains keyed state to support that computation.
But a fraud-scoring service also needs to retrieve the result. Flink’s internal state isn’t designed for general-purpose serving, and Flink deprecated its Queryable State feature in 1.18. A common solution is to publish the count to Redis.
That gives applications a dedicated serving layer, with its own scaling and operational requi…

The early rush to encourage employees to use AI wherever possible led to a new way of measuring productivity based on the consumption of AI tokens, or technically the underlying AI foundation model tokens. Employees who did not use AI were immediately visible through their AI consumption bill, or lack thereof, while high consumption was treated as a positive signal. The number of tokens consumed became a badge of honor.
For a while, more AI usage suggested more productivity and innovation. Some organizations even began treating AI activity as a proxy for employee engagement. This led to the phenomenon of ‘tokenmaxxing’, with the unintended consequence of AI costs growing out of control and raising a more difficult question: what does successful AI adoption actually look like and how do you measure it?
General Manager for ITSG at GoTo.
The latest Pulse of Work 2026 research points to the gap between adoption and value. Of the 7.7 million individuals potentially affected, 5.8 million are current and former platform members who had their names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, gender information, and encrypted passwords compromised.

The findings, presented by Césaire A. Meh, Manager of Private Markets at the IFC during the Africa Financial Industry Summit (AFIS) in Luanda, Angola, examine the factors driving corporate borrowing costs across countries, currencies, and financial markets.

None of that is a knock on the people who built real careers doing that work well. The work is simply moving to the agents, and the value is moving to a different skillset, faster than anyone handed out a plan for it.
The professionals who come out ahead will be the ones who retrain early, and the rest are left against the wall, not because they stood still, but because no one told them what to run toward.
This is what GRC Agentification actually means. Not AI assisting a human who still does the work, but AI agents doing the work while the human moves up a level to direct and govern them.
It is a far bigger shift than "adopt AI" makes it sound, and the guidance most professionals get stops right at the slogan. So here is the part nobody is spelling out: the three skills that separate the managers whose roles get automated away from the managers who start running the agents.
All three are learnable, and the time to start is now: context, agent governance, and communication.

Autrement dit, le message est refusé parce que le domaine de l’expéditeur ne présente pas les enregistrements d’authentification nécessaires, ou, plus précisément, parce que Microsoft ne parvient pas à valider suffisamment son identité.
Dès le lendemain, plusieurs acteurs du secteur ont commencé à lancer l’alerte et à détailler les mesures permettant de contourner ce blocage.
Trois réglages pour prouver qu’un mail est authentique
Ce durcissement repose sur un enjeu de sécurité : rien n’empêche techniquement d’envoyer un mail en se faisant passer pour quelqu’un d’autre, c’est précisément ce qui facilite le phishing.
Et si le message de Microsoft peut sembler cryptique, il renvoie en réalité aux trois mécanismes qui permettent au destinataire de vérifier l’origine d’un message :
- SPF indique quels serveurs sont autorisés à envoyer des mails au nom d’un domaine.
- DKIM ajoute une signature numérique à chaque message, afin de prouver qu’il n’a pas été altéré en route.
- DMARC vérifie enfin que ces contrôles correspondent bien au domaine affiché dans l’adresse de l’expéditeur, celle que voit le destinataire.

articles.title: Why semantic layers will be essential for enterprise AI
articles.summary:
Why semantic layers will be essential for enterprise AI
AI can find your data. It can’t read your mind. AI agents can already reach into your CRM, your warehouse, and your ERP, and with standards like MCP, that list keeps growing. Access is solved. Understanding is not. An agent can retrieve every record in your pipeline and still give your CRO the wrong answer, not because the data is bad, but because it doesn’t know what you mean by “pipeline.” Agents without semantics don’t fail loudly. They deliver confident answers to the wrong question.
“Pipeline” means something different at every company
Ask an executive, “How is pipeline looking this quarter?” and it sounds like a simple request. It isn’t. The answer depends on your sales stages, your forecasting methodology, your territory structure, and your qualification criteria, which are business rules that evolved over years, often without ever being written down. Two companies can use the same word and mean entirely different things. Businesses don’t run on raw data. They run on shared meaning, and humans carry that meaning around in their heads. Agents don’t have heads. They have whatever we give them.
From systems of record to systems of agency

El aire acondicionado es el único equipo capaz de bajar activamente la temperatura de una habitación sofocante, mientras que el ventilador aporta alivio inmediato a una fracción del costo de compra y consumo eléctrico.
Entender el funcionamiento de cada tecnología, su efecto en la factura de luz y las condiciones del espacio donde se instalan resulta determinante para decidir qué equipo conviene este verano.
Diferencias entre aire acondicionado y ventilador para refrescar ambientes
El punto de partida para comparar ambos sistemas es el principio físico que utilizan. El aire acondicionado trabaja mediante un circuito de refrigeración por compresión: extrae el calor y la humedad del aire interior y los expulsa al exterior a través de un condensador, para devolver después aire frío al ambiente. Es el único de los dos dispositivos que logra reducir la temperatura real de una estancia.
El ventilador, en cambio, no enfría el aire en ningún momento. Su función consiste en generar una corriente que acelera la evaporación del sudor sobre la piel, lo que produce una sensación térmica de entre 2 °C y 4 °C menos (entre 3,6 °F y 7,2 °F) respecto a la temperatura real.

articles.title: Hackers exploit SSHole OpenSSH flaw to breach Linux systems
articles.summary:
Hackers are actively exploiting the "SSHole" vulnerability (CVE-2026-123158) in OpenSSH to execute commands, steal credentials, and establish persistent access.
Multiple cybersecurity firms have confirmed the attacks, reporting that exploitation attempts began on November 5, the day a proof-of-concept exploit became available, with successful exploitation recorded the following day.
Disclosed by security researcher Ozgun Kultekin last week, SSHole allows bypassing authentication in OpenSSH running on certain musl-based Linux systems, including the lightweight Alpine distribution used in cloud and virtual environments.
The flaw lets attackers log in to accounts with a password hash is set to an asterisk (*) to prevent password logins.
An oversized password causes musl’s password-hashing function to return * on error, which OpenSSH mistakenly treats as a match for the account’s stored value.
Kultekin explained that exploitation requires specific authentication settings, does not affect accounts with valid password hashes, and can lead to root access where the compromised account has passwordless administrative privileges.
OpenSSH maintainers fixed the vulnerability in version 10.6p2 released on November 5, while exploit code became available roughly four hours later.
Finnish security company Defused said over the weekend that it had observed "a small amount of actors" trying to exploit SSHole, although the activity was not widespread.

articles.title: Uber launches parking service following SpotHero acquisition, with an eye on robotaxis | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Uber on Monday said it is launching a new service that lets customers reserve and pay for parking in major U.S. cities, about nine months after the ride-hailing company acquired parking app SpotHero.
The acquisition, announced back in February, gives Uber access to a network of 13,000 garages, lots, and valet services across more than 400 cities, the company said. And while Uber’s initial plans will focus on human drivers, the company also plans to leverage these parking spots to help the dozens of autonomous vehicle companies it has partnered with.
Uber said the parking spots could be used as staging and waiting locations for autonomous vehicles to help reduce congestion and deadheading, which refers to the miles a vehicle travels without a paying passenger or cargo on board.
For now, the company plans to focus on commuters driving their own vehicles. Uber said it will initially launch in 15 U.S. cities, including Atlanta, Austin, Boston, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, Nashville, New York City, Philadelphia, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington, DC.
Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi indicated earlier this month that the company wants the app to be more relevant to commuters.
“Commute is one of our largest categories,” he said during Uber’s third-quarter earnings call. “And to be able to offer commuters an Uber to work, a pass to avoid surge, and parking if they want it when they want to drive is a great example of us building out our inventory of services…

articles.summary:
Cuando se habla de seguridad en Windows 11, la mayoría de las miradas suelen centrarse en Microsoft Defender. Smart App Control, o Control Inteligente de Aplicaciones, es una nueva función de seguridad que llegó con Windows 11. La herramienta utiliza la inteligencia en la nube de Microsoft para encontrar si una aplicación es segura y se puede ejecutar en tu ordenador. Si vienes de Windows 10, esta función reemplaza a SmartScreen, una función que protegía tu equipo ante programas y descargas de dudosa procedencia.

El objetivo es determinar si una aplicación es confiable antes de permitir que se ejecute, lo que reduce el riesgo de que una amenaza comprometa nuestro sistema. A diferencia de su predecesor, Smart App Control bloquea por defecto aplicaciones sin firmar o desconocidas y es necesario desactivarlo por completo si quieres ejecutarlas.

articles.title: Plex2Shell Exploited Against QNAP NAS Users
articles.summary:
Threat actors are exploiting Plex2Shell to hack into Plex Media Server applications on QNAP NAS devices, Taiwanese storage and networking solutions provider QNAP warns.
Plex2Shell is a chain of four vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655 and CVE-2026-96656) in Plex Media Server that was patched this summer.
Widespread exploitation of the four-flaw chain started in mid-October, after technical details and proof-of-concept (PoC) code were published.
Successful exploitation of Plex2Shell does not require valid credentials and could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code on exposed servers, with the privileges of the Plex service.
Plex Media Server is available as a third-party application to QNAP NAS users, through the official App Center.
“QNAP has received reports from some users that Plex Media Server on their NAS appears to have been compromised through these vulnerabilities,” the Taiwanese firm warned on Friday.
“The QNAP Technical Support team is assisting affected users and has confirmed that no data loss has occurred. The QNAP Product Security Incident Response Team (QNAP PSIRT) has confirmed that the vulnerabilities exist only in Plex Media Server; QTS, QuTS hero, and other QNAP operating systems are not themselves affected,” it added.
QNAP NAS users are advised to update to Plex Media Server version 1.43.3 or later as soon as possible.

An investigation by Bloomberg and Type Investigations earlier this year reported that BusPatrol equipped around 35,000 buses across 24 states. Its cameras flag suspected illegal passing, with police reviewing evidence before tickets are issued.
In Montgomery County, Maryland, the investigation tallied more than 375,000 tickets and $92 million in issued fines. Those are some stunning figures, but the research found little reduction in violations and no evidence of fewer collisions near stopped buses.
Between fiscal years 2019 and 2024, the county retained around $18.5 million from collected fines while setting aside roughly $40 million for manufacturer BusPatrol. The company says its financial arrangements cover installation and operating costs, and that it absorbs shortfalls when camera expenses exceed violation revenue.

articles.title: Money Fellows took an old savings habit and built a business
articles.summary:
The global tech industry likes an old habit best when it can kill it. Cash is going. Brick-and-mortar branches are finished. The informal economy is waiting to be formalised, and all it takes is a platform and a convincing pitch.
That was Ahmed Wadi’s proposition in 2016. Egyptians already had a way to save and borrow. They pooled money, took turns collecting it, and relied on social obligation to keep everyone paying. The arrangement had survived without venture capital funding or a credit engine that powers modern finance.
Perhaps it deserved an upgrade.
Ten years after Wadi began building Money Fellows, an Egyptian fintech, much of its work has involved discovering how difficult that idea becomes when participants no longer know one another.
And, having attracted over one million registrations, the company has only recently taken its model beyond Egypt, into Morocco, with ambitions to explore more markets in the coming years.
Looking at Africa’s fintech ecosystem in the past decade, there are faster ways to grow a company’s operating markets. But Wadi wanted to understand the business first.
“We were very focused on really understanding and cracking the model on a local scale before we start distracting ourselves and launching other countries,” he recalled in an interview with TechCabal.
This sounds sensible. It also sounds considerably easier in retrospect.
An old habit, a new business

articles.title: Single-shot and agentic retrieval with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Single-shot and agentic retrieval with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
A banking operations employee starts the morning by asking an internal AI assistant which documents are needed to open a business account. The answer is in a single checklist. A few hours later, the same employee asks how those requirements differ across sole proprietorships, LLCs, and partnerships with multiple owners. That answer is spread across several policy guides. One assistant has to handle both questions, quickly and cheaply for the first and thoroughly for the second. Applications need a way to match retrieval effort to each request without building separate systems for simple and complex questions.
Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports single-shot Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and retrieval-only requests through AgenticRetrieveStream. With single-shot RAG, the service searches your knowledge bases once and uses a foundation model (FM) to generate an answer from the passages it finds. With retrieval-only requests, the service returns the matching passages without generating an answer, so your application or the user can work with the source text directly. These modes join the existing agentic retrieval, where the service plans and runs multiple searches before answering. You can now use the same API for both of the employee’s questions: single-shot RAG for the checklist lookup and agentic retrieval for the cross-policy comparison.

articles.title: Revolve Puts Data Breach Victim Count at 1.5 Million
articles.summary:
Online fashion retailer Revolve has informed the Indiana Attorney General’s Office that 1,515,073 individuals were impacted by the data breach it disclosed in October.
The company revealed the incident on October 29 in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). It started sending notification letters to impacted customers around the same time.
Revolve had not publicly shared a total. Its notices to regulators in Iowa, Massachusetts, South Carolina, Texas, and Vermont covered roughly 197,000 people combined.
The retailer says an unauthorized party broke into some of its systems, including its e-commerce platform, on September 11. Per the Indiana Attorney General’s records, Revolve became aware of the intrusion on September 29.
According to the company, the intruder may have relied on “automated means” to collect customers’ names and contact information, including mailing addresses, along with their card numbers and expiration dates.
The exposure is limited to shoppers who chose to store a payment method in their online accounts.
Revolve reported the attack to federal law enforcement and enlisted external cybersecurity experts to help with its response.
The company has yet to explain how the hackers got into its systems. So far, the attack has not been publicly claimed by any hacker group.

articles.title: Chrome Update Patches Exploited XML Zero-Day, Eighth This Year
articles.summary:
Google on Monday informed Chrome users of new security updates that patch nine vulnerabilities, including a zero-day exploited in the wild.
The exploited vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-125350 and rated high severity, is a use-after-free in the web browser’s XML component.
A researcher who wants to remain anonymous reported the issue to Google on November 6.
The tech giant has not shared any additional details, and no information appears to be available on the attacks exploiting CVE-2026-125350.
CISA has yet to add CVE-2026-125350 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
This is the eighth Chrome zero-day exploited this year after CVE-2026-2441, CVE-2026-3909, CVE-2026-3910, CVE-2026-5281, CVE-2026-11645, CVE-2026-85046, and CVE-2026-87491.
In addition to the zero-day, the latest Chrome updates patch six high-severity vulnerabilities in the WebGL, FileSystem, Compositing, GPU, V8, and XML components. Google discovered most of the flaws internally.
Two medium-severity bugs described as uninitialized resource issues in the GPU component have also been fixed.
The patches are included in Chrome 157 updates, specifically versions 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Mac, and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux.

Topcoat, a modular full-stack framework for Rust built by the Tokio team, has moved out of private development with a public GitHub repository, a v0.9 release, and a series of blog posts outlining its direction. The project is positioned as a batteries-included web framework that stays entirely server-rendered, with reactivity added through cross-compiled Rust expressions rather than WebAssembly.
Topcoat introduces several ideas, including a view! macro for mixing HTML with Rust control flow, module-based routing inferred from the project's file tree, an asset pipeline with content-hashed URLs, and a Tailwind integration that works without Node.js. It also announces tighter integration with the Toasty async ORM, which handles migrations and database access in the same Rust workspace.
One of the headline design choices in Topcoat is the $(...) expression. These are ordinary type-checked Rust fragments that Topcoat evaluates on the server for the initial render and also translates to JavaScript, so they re-run instantly in the browser without a WASM bundle or separate client build step.
When an update does need the server, developers can mark a component as a #[shard]. Topcoat re-renders the shard on the server whenever one of its $(...) arguments changes, then swaps the new HTML into the page, giving a similar feel to reactive updates without shipping a client-side router. This positions Topcoat closer to HTMX, Datastar and Phoenix LiveView than to React or SolidJS.

The climate case for AI has not been made
AI leaders claim their tech will fix the climate. The evidence mostly points in the opposite direction so far.
This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on countries to commit to ensuring that AI is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action.
But so far, industries around the world aren’t doing nearly enough to harness the technology to actually drive down the greenhouse-gas emissions heating up the planet, despite some very optimistic claims from AI companies.
In 2024, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman declared that AI would unleash “astounding triumphs,” including “fixing the climate.” The year before, in a 2023 op-ed, the head of sustainability at Google and her coauthor wrote that AI could reduce global emissions 5% to 10% by 2030.
Some academic researchers have examined these AI-related climate claims. Google’s eighth-generation TPU announcement on Monday included more than new chips, introducing TPU Sync, an open-source system designed to speed up AI inference by tackling a problem that worsens as context windows grow: moving data between different types of memory.
The software is made for developers running large models, particularly ones handling million-token contexts and reinforcement-learning workloads. The company claims it can cut KV-cache transfer latency and time to first token by more than 90% in some tests.

Inside the memory hierarchy
Written in C++, the framework moves data between accelerator memory, host DRAM, storage, and the network. It uses zero-copy transfers and native PjRtBuffer hardware descriptors to avoid unnecessary copies.

AMD Confirms Excessive SSD Writes in Radeon Drivers, Fix Coming with Adrenalin 26.11.1
AMD has confirmed that the current versions of Radeon drivers, Adrenalin 26.10.1 and Adrenalin 26.10.2, are experiencing an issue that causes excessive SSD writing. This problem results in the SSD writing dozens of gigabytes of data unnecessarily. The culprit appears to be AMD's External Events Client Module, which runs under the name atieclxx.exe on Windows systems. This module is causing some users' system drives to be constantly busy with writes. Reports indicate that the write rate ranges from 0.3 MB/s to 1.5 MB/s, with one Reddit user reporting sustained activity at 5 MB/s. The process is part of AMD's External Events Utility, which manages tasks such as detecting monitors and responding to Radeon software hotkeys. Unfortunately, it has entered an infinite loop of data writing.

In short, reballed memory refers to used memory salvaged from old hardware and fitted with new solder balls so they can be installed on other devices.

articles.title: How Milsat built Nigeria’s digital address system
articles.summary:
For years, finding an address across much of Nigeria has depended far less on a number than on a description. A visitor might be directed to a street, told to look for a distinctive building, instructed to turn at a familiar shop, or advised to keep walking until reaching a landmark tree. Delivery riders often know a neighbourhood intimately yet still struggle to identify the correct front gate. Across the country, the gap between arriving in a community and reaching a specific doorway remains considerable.
Nigeria’s new digital postcode system is designed to narrow that gap. Launched on October 1, 2026, it moves beyond the traditional postcode, which identifies a broad area, to assign codes at the level of individual buildings or delivery units. The ambition is to make it possible to identify a particular building with greater precision, whether it is in a busy city, a developing suburb or a rural community.
But the system is more than a new set of numbers and letters. Behind it is an attempt to build a national location-data infrastructure: a system that can collect information about buildings, verify it, update it as places change and make it useful to government agencies, businesses and ordinary Nigerians.
For Taslim Salaudeen, Milsat’s chief executive and co-founder, the project is about something bigger than giving building codes.

articles.title: France blames Iranian hackers for supermarket attacks that sparked fires
articles.summary:
France has linked October cyberattacks that disrupted refrigeration systems at more than 700 supermarkets and other retail locations to Iranian state-backed hackers, saying the attacks caused food losses and sparked at least 15 fires.
In a statement issued Monday, France's Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs blamed the attacks on Shahid Kaveh, a cyber-offensive unit affiliated with the electronic and cyber center of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
"France condemns in the strongest possible terms the unacceptable cyberattacks carried out on its territory by the Islamic Republic of Iran against its interests," reads the statement.
The attacks occurred overnight on October 11–12, when hackers compromised industrial refrigeration controllers and remotely changed defrost settings to high temperatures, disrupting systems used to preserve food.
As BleepingComputer reported, the attacks affected an estimated 250 to 350 French supermarkets, forcing stores to discard fresh and frozen products.
French authorities have now revealed that approximately 700 retail locations were targeted, with the cyberattacks causing at least 15 fires.
A technical report published by France's CERT-FR says Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché, along with smaller butcher shops, a slaughterhouse, and cooperative food-processing facilities, were affected by the attacks.

The model delivers more power than typical solar home systems while needing less infrastructure than conventional mini-grids.

The US$7 million financing from BII, the UK’s development finance institution and impact investor, will allow it to procure equipment for roughly 150,000 new connections, a more than tenfold increase, with the potential to bring electricity to 750,000 people in rural Nigeria for the first time.
The facility tackles a key barrier to scaling distributed renewable energy – access to flexible working capital. By buying inputs upfront and in larger volumes, Okra expects to cut equipment costs and shorten delivery times to Nigeria from four months to about two.

Radeon drivers may be quietly racking up thousands of gigabytes in SSD writes
An SSD can spend most of its day doing very little, particularly when a PC is sitting idle. That may not be the case for some AMD Radeon systems, however, with reports suggesting that AMD’s External Events Utility (EEU), which is installed alongside Radeon drivers, may be writing data to the system driver continuously, even when the computer is barely being used. The issue drew attention again on November 8, when Reddit user ‘darklinkpower’ highlighted reports of the unusual drive activity.
One Radeon owner claimed the problem had been quietly eating into their drive's reported health for more than a year, writing: "I just found out that the driver eats up 1% of my SSD health every month for 16 months." Another user reported sustained writes of approximately 5MB/s while their PC was idle. Another one claimed their SSD health had dropped by about 1% every month for 16 months. On Monday, it announced a $240 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and co-led by Insight Partners.

A comienzos de los años 70 se empezaron a tirar neumáticos usados junto al condado de Broward (Florida). Se trataba de un arrecife artificial. En total se lanzaron entre uno y dos millones de neumáticos. Se pretendía conseguir así un mayor hábitat para peces y disponer de un sitio para estos residuos. Más de medio siglo después todavía están en pleno proceso de retiro.
Se trata del Osborne Tire Reef. Se lanzaron en una zona de arena entre dos arrecifes naturales. Cercano hay otro arrecife artificial (Osborne Reef) de estructuras de hormigón. En el informe de Florida se diferencian los dos.
En el mismo momento de su vertido comenzaron los problemas de inestabilidad. Algunas de las cintas que mantenían unidos los grupos se rompieron en la propia descarga. Además, los cierres metálicos se corroían y las cintas se iban soltando. También las corrientes y el oleaje de las tormentas han provocado que se hayan ido arrastrando hacia los arrecifes próximos.
En el plan de restauración (con los estudios de 2019 y 2024) se estimaron unos 521.000 neumáticos superficiales (no enterrados) en las zonas analizadas. articles.title: York University breach exposed personal information dating to 2007
articles.summary:
York University in Toronto has confirmed that a threat actor breached its systems and accessed personal information submitted through online forms.
The unauthorized access was discovered on October 25 and affected forms submitted on 14 university websites between 2007 and 2026.
York University is a major university based in Toronto, Canada, with more than 55,700 students across 200 undergraduate and graduate degree programs, and an administrative staff of 7,000.
“York was recently subject to a cybersecurity incident involving an unauthorized actor accessing limited online forms used by University departments,” the university stated on Friday.
“While York acted quickly to contain the incident following discovery, we regret to confirm the theft of personal information from some departmental forms.”
The announcement lists the exposed data in detail, by category. Across the affected forms, the attacker accessed the following:
- Email address
- Phone number
- Date of birth
- York identification number
- Government ID information
- Third-party contact information
- Health information
- Academic history
- Employment history
- Financial status
- Criminal background
- Demographic details
- Photos and other images
The exact data types exposed vary by person, and most stolen records contained basic contact information and York ID numbers, the university said.

articles.title: MENA startup funding plunges 96% to $40 million in October 2026 as megadeals dry up
articles.summary:
MENA startup funding plunges 96% to $40 million in October 2026 as megadeals dry up
Startup investment across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) plunged in October 2026, with 32 startups raising just $40 million, as the absence of large funding rounds brought September’s short-lived rebound to an abrupt halt.
The total represents a 96% month-on-month decline from the $1.1 billion raised in September and a 95% drop from the $784.9 million recorded in October 2025, making October one of the weakest months for regional startup funding this year.
The sharp reversal underscores the volatility of MENA’s investment landscape, where a handful of outsized transactions can dramatically reshape monthly funding figures. September’s performance was heavily driven by three Saudi fintech deals worth a combined $762.5 million, accounting for nearly 70% of the month’s total.
October offered a starkly different picture. With no megadeals or later-stage rounds to lift the headline figure, funding remained concentrated in smaller, early-stage transactions, reflecting a more cautious investment environment amid persistent geopolitical and economic uncertainty.
Yet the slowdown was not uniform. Saudi Arabia maintained its lead, fintech continued to attract investor activity, and business-to-business (B2B) startups secured the overwhelming majority of available capital.

articles.title: Microsoft is making Windows keyboard accessibility features less annoying
articles.summary:
Something to look forward to: Windows is finally changing how users interact with two of the operating system's most prominent accessibility features. Sticky Keys and Filter Keys, first introduced in Windows 95, will soon be easier to disable permanently. As a result, users who don't have trouble interacting with a keyboard should experience fewer interruptions during critical tasks – or, perhaps more importantly, leisure activities.
Sticky Keys is a classic accessibility feature available across all major computer operating systems. System 6 reportedly introduced the feature on Mac systems in 1988. The option provides a way to "serialize" keystrokes, allowing them to press and release a modifier key – Shift, Ctrl, Alt, or Win – just once when using a standard keyboard shortcut, rather than holding it down while pressing another key.
Filter Keys, meanwhile, is a Windows-specific accessibility option designed to ignore brief or repeated keystrokes. People affected by hand tremors or other physical conditions can benefit greatly from this feature, which helps prevent typing and other input errors.
Both features are designed to improve accessibility in Windows, but they can also become a nuisance if you don't need them. Traditionally, these options can be activated by simply pressing the Shift key five times or holding it down for an extended period. articles.title: Distributed LLM Inference on Kubernetes with llm-d, Wasm, & TornadoVM
articles.summary:
In this episode, Edoardo Vacchi discusses the evolving landscape of WebAssembly on the backend, running Java workloads on GPUs using TornadoVM, and optimizing distributed AI inference using llm-d and vLLM on Kubernetes. Edoardo explains how llm-d manages cache locality (KV and prefix caches), request routing, and batch inference across Kubernetes clusters to maximize expensive GPU utilization.
Key Takeaways
- Wasm has matured into a backend runtime for sandboxing, cross-language compilation, and workload migration between browsers and end-user devices.
- TornadoVM allows developers to compile and run Java code directly on GPU backends, enabling projects like GPU-accelerated Llama 3 written entirely in Java.
- While vLLM optimizes high-throughput inference on a single instance via PagedAttention, llm-d extends this across Kubernetes clusters to manage multi-node distributed inference.
- Traditional Kubernetes load balancers break LLM efficiency; llm-d balances staying with the same instance to leverage cached conversational context while preventing node overload.
- llm-d introduces batch inference during idle cluster periods and semantic classification to route prompts to right-sized, cost-effective models without sacrificing privacy.

articles.title: Auf dem Trockenen? Wo es gravierende Datenlücken bei unserem Grundwasser gibt
articles.summary:
Datenlücken beim Grundwasser: „Wir wissen mehr über die Mondoberfläche als über unser Trinkwasser“
Kein Plätschern, kein Rauschen, keine Ferienromantik: Unser Grundwasser ist der wohl unauffälligste Gewässertyp, dafür ein ausgesprochen mächtiger. Rund 23 Billionen Kubikmeter H₂O – eine Zahl mit 15 Nullen – schlummern unter der Oberfläche unseres Planeten. Das entspricht etwa 99 Prozent der flüssigen Süßwasservorräte weltweit. Der Wasserspeicher unter Tage gilt als eine der wichtigsten Ressourcen, um die Wasserversorgung in der Klimakrise zu sichern – auch in Deutschland.
Doch die Begehrlichkeiten sind groß. Unsere Wasserwerke gewinnen rund 70 Prozent des Trinkwassers aus der Tiefe. Auch die Industrie, der Bergbau, die Landwirtschaft und etliche Menschen mit Eigenheim und Garten nutzen Grundwasser. „Gerade sind die Entnahmen recht konstant, wir rechnen aber mit einer Steigerung in den nächsten Jahren“, sagt Bernd Kirschbaum vom Umweltbundesamt. Unter anderem, weil Rechenzentren und Wasserstoffproduzenten künftig zunehmend Grundwasser zapfen werden. Auch Pflanzen konsumieren immer mehr, denn bei höheren Temperaturen und längeren Vegetationsperioden steigt die Verdunstung über ihre Blätter.
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 8/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns mit den Folgen des Klimawandels und wie wir uns an Hitze, Dürre und Überschwemmungen anpassen sollten. Das Heft ist seit dem 06.11.2026 im Zeitschriftenhandel und in unserem Online-Shop erhältlic…

Paramount Skydance’s CEO compared AI to CGI, but said it ‘will never be a replacement’ for artists.

That technology gave birth to amazing stories like Jurassic Park and Terminator 2, and it’s hard to imagine that AI is not going to have a more significant impact than that. articles.title: AWS Launches TorchNeuron to Run PyTorch Models on AWS Trainium Without Modifications
articles.summary:
At the recent PyTorch Conference North America 2026, Amazon introduced TorchNeuron, a native PyTorch backend that enables developers to run existing PyTorch code on AWS Trainium AI chips with virtually no code modifications.
Beyond reducing engineering effort, TorchNeuron allows enterprises to share hardware capacity between training and inference workloads, reallocating resources from inference to training during off-peak hours.
Amazon says that a single configuration change is sufficient to switch hardware, eliminating the need to rewrite and revalidate models when moving to Trainium.
Today, 85% of AI researchers and developers write their code in PyTorch. Until now, the hardware that code could run on was far more limited than the code itself, and expanding to new chips meant rewriting and revalidating work that took months to perfect.
According to the TorchNeuron documentations, when leveraging PyTorch's automatic device detection through torch.accelerator, the only required change is replacing .to('cuda') to .to('neuron'). The backend also natively supports distributed training and PyTorch parallelism APIs, including DDP, FSDP2, DTensor, and others. In addition, TorchNeuron provides native support for Torch streams and events through torch_neuronx.Stream and torch_neuronx.Event.

articles.title: F1 in Brazil: You’ve got to keep your tires alive
articles.summary:
In sports, a “dead rubber” is a match that takes place after the outcome of the series or championship has already been decided. The people in charge hate this*—if you wrap up a title two-thirds of the way through a season, the viewers evaporate, as there’s nothing left at stake. But anyone who decided to skip this year’s Brazilian Grand Prix this past weekend missed one of the year’s most entertaining races, as a combination of a mixed-up starting order, some very fast drivers at the back, and a wet track that dried and then saw rain again resulted in action aplenty.
A peculiarity of F1 is that even if you manage to win a championship, there’s no guarantee you’ll be in a position to defend it. Take McLaren’s Lando Norris, who took the crown in 2025 after a nail-biting fight with his teammate Oscar Piastri and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen. Sadly for Lando, McLaren did not start this year in a position to win races, and even with several upgrades, the team has produced a car that is still very tricky to drive. But this weekend in Brazil, Norris demonstrated the form that earned him the number 1.
Rain on Saturday during qualifying helped jumble the usual running order. It was heavy enough that drivers used the wet weather tire with deep treads, which usually generates so much spray that visibility disappears and running has to be suspended. articles.title: Suecia tiñe de magenta sus paneles solares y consigue cosechar debajo el mismo brócoli que a pleno sol, aunque tarda 25 días más en crecer
articles.summary:
El brócoli que se ha desarrollado bajo estos paneles semitransparentes de color magenta ha sido similar en tamaño final al que se encuentra en pleno sol. Sin embargo, se han necesitado 25 días más para llegar a la madurez. Así lo han demostrado en un ensayo en Suecia (Universidad de Mälardalen).
Los paneles permiten que llegue cierta luz a las plantas. Con parte del resto se genera electricidad. Se han diseñado para que pasen las longitudes de onda en rojo y azul (que son las que absorben los pigmentos de la clorofila). De esta manera se trata de paliar el problema de la sombra que puede reducir la disponibilidad de luz.
Dos transparencias y una cosecha más tarde
Los investigadores han comparado el brócoli de una parcela sin cubrir con otros dos casos de brócoli bajo módulos con transparencia nominal del 50 % y un 70 %. Han medido variables ambientales y los resultados de rendimiento y composición nutricional e incluso han analizado la respuesta fotosintética.
Se obtuvo una eficiencia en el uso de la radiación 4,5 veces mayor que a pleno sol en el caso de los paneles del 50 % y 2,8 veces en el caso de los del 70 %. Este parámetro mide la relación entre la biomasa seca aérea obtenida y la radiación fotosintéticamente activa recibida. Se ha conseguido un resultado similar de cosecha con menor luz. Sin embargo, se ha tenido que esperar 25 días más.

articles.title: SEGA newsletter data breach exposes 2.2 million email addresses
articles.summary:
Japanese gaming giant SEGA has disclosed that a data breach at its third-party newsletter provider, ARARA, exposed the email addresses of 2.2 million newsletter subscribers.
The company says the exposed data also includes 92,300 records with additional information yet to be determined. The breach affects 11 newsletters linked to SEGA and SEGA Fave products and services.
The investigation found that the compromised data did not include customer names, dates of birth, gender, addresses, phone numbers, credit card details, or account passwords.
Also, email addresses registered with a “SEGA Account” are handled by a separate distribution system and were not affected by this incident.
The company is working with ARARA to determine what data was exposed and says it has no confirmed evidence of misuse.
“We are currently investigating the information associated with newsletter distribution in cooperation with ARARA,” SEGA stated.
ARARA service breached
ARARA disclosed on November 2 that it suffered a massive breach affecting its email distribution service, which compromised 77 million email addresses from nearly 380 corporate clients.
According to the company, a web server vulnerability and problems in its system environment contributed to the incident, but the exact intrusion method and timing remain under investigation.
ARARA previously estimated a smaller impact and assured SEGA on October 29 that no data compromise had occurred.

articles.title: WhatsApp, Signal, Messenger... : la France renonce à forcer l’accès aux conversations chiffrées
articles.summary:
En 2025, le gouvernement français a introduit une proposition de loi contre le narcotrafic. Celle-ci prévoyait notamment d’obliger les plateformes de messagerie, comme WhatsApp, Signal ou encore Messenger, à transmettre aux autorités les conversations, pourtant chiffrées, de certaines personnes surveillées. À la suite de nombreuses contestations, la mesure n’a pas été conservée dans la loi promulguée contre le narcotrafic. Le débat a ensuite été relancé avec l’introduction de l’article 16 bis dans le projet de loi sur la résilience des infrastructures critiques et le renforcement de la cybersécurité. Pour rappel, l’article 16 bis vise à interdire d’imposer aux plateformes de messagerie des portes dérobées permettant aux autorités d’accéder à certaines conversations pourtant chiffrées de bout en bout.
Accès à des conversations chiffrées : le gouvernement veut un compromis
Le conflit autour de l’article 16 bis est simple. D’un côté, les services de renseignement veulent son abolition pour pouvoir accéder à certaines discussions chiffrées, dans le cadre d’affaires sensibles ou criminelles. De l’autre côté, les plateformes de messagerie, mais aussi une bonne partie de leurs utilisateurs, veulent maintenir la promesse de discussions totalement confidentielles, inaccessibles à l’État. Toute la nuance de cette affaire réside dans la capacité des autorités à accéder aux conversations chiffrées. Où commence et où s’arrête la surveillance des individus ?

articles.title: YouTube streaming data returns to Billboard charts, ending major disagreement | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
YouTube is officially returning to the Billboard charts, ending a disagreement over how music streams should count toward chart rankings.
Announced Monday, YouTube is set to resume sharing its streaming data with Billboard in 2027. The decision follows recent changes to Billboard’s chart formula, which now gives more weight to ad-supported streams.
The disagreement began in December 2025, when YouTube said it would stop sharing its streaming data with Billboard. The company argued that the chart formula favored paid subscriptions while not giving enough credit to fans who listen for free with ads.
At the time, Lyor Cohen, YouTube’s global head of music, criticized the system in a blog post, saying it didn’t reflect how people listen to music today.
“Billboard uses an outdated formula that weights subscription-supported streams higher than ad-supported. This doesn’t reflect how fans engage with music today and ignores the massive engagement from fans who don’t have a subscription. Streaming is the primary way people experience music, making up 84% of U.S. recorded music revenue,” Cohen wrote.
Under Billboard’s previous formula, 1,000 paid streams counted the same as 2,500 ad-supported streams. YouTube felt this gave too much importance to paid listening, especially when millions of fans discover and support artists through free streaming.
Billboard has now updated its formula, reducing the gap between the two types of streams. Under the new system, 1,000 paid streams will equa…

articles.summary:
Huawei develops 'entirely Chinese' homegrown desktop PC system — features 10-core, 20-thread Kirin X90 consumer CPU and Huawei's own HarmonyOS operating system, but Western supply chain lingers
Goodbye, Wintel? Software for Windows too?
Huawei has introduced its first desktop PCs powered by its own 10-core processor as well as proprietary HarmonyOS operating system, reports the Southern China Morning Post. articles.title: Many PCs from '80s and '90s had keyhole locks, right next to the Turbo and Reset buttons. What was it for?
articles.summary:
And now, for some context
An actual key: The 1980s answer to pressing "Win+L"
If you ever cracked open a beige 386 or 486 tower, you might remember a keyhole on the front panel, usually parked near the Turbo and Reset buttons. IBM called it the keylock. With the key turned to "locked," the PC stopped listening to the keyboard. It was a physical password.
The reason it existed is explained by the software of the time. Early IBM-compatible PCs ran MS-DOS, a single-user system with no accounts and no passwords. Anyone who sat down at your desk could browse your files (or delete them) with a keypress.
IBM had already used keylocks on its mainframes and servers, and in 1984 it brought the idea to the IBM PC AT (model 5170), an expensive 286-based machine that cost thousands of dollars (over $12,500 in today's money). The AT shipped with a tubular pin-tumbler lock, similar to the "Ace" locks found on vending machines, pinball tables, and alarm panels. PC Magazine described it as a way for executives to sleep at night.
On that IBM, the lock did several things: it blocked the keyboard at the controller level, so software couldn't work around it. If the machine was powered on while locked, the BIOS self-test halted, and a metal piece inside the case moved into place to stop the cover from being removed. IBM also sold a separate "Keylock Option" for the original PC and XT that went further and blocked the machine from powering on at all.
Compatibility was the selling point of PC clones…
